What happens if I move out of Canada while I have an active personal loan with CIBC?

If you are no longer a resident of Canada, CIBC may end your loan agreement without your permission. Additionally, you must immediately pay all amounts owing under the loan, regardless of whether they are currently due, and you are responsible for paying any applicable withholding taxes. (cibc_personal_loan.pdf, p.8)

How is the interest on my CIBC personal loan calculated and applied to my balance?

Interest is calculated daily by multiplying your outstanding principal balance by the daily interest factor based on the current interest rate. The daily charges are then added together for the statement period to determine the total monthly interest. This interest is compounded monthly, meaning unpaid interest from the previous month is added to your loan balance, and the bank may charge interest on that interest. (cibc_personal_loan.pdf, p.5)

Are electronic records and instructions provided to the bank considered final proof of my agreements and transactions?

Yes, electronic records and instructions are considered final and conclusive evidence of the information and your agreements, provided there is no manifest or clerical error on the bank's part. (cimb_personal_loan.pdf, p.11)

Can CIBC take money from my other bank accounts to cover costs related to my personal loan agreement?

Yes. If you owe money under this indemnity clause and do not have a credit balance on your loan, CIBC may take funds from any of your other accounts with them or their affiliates—including joint accounts—to satisfy the claim, though they cannot take money from your registered retirement savings plan (RRSP) or registered retirement income fund (RRIF). (cibc_personal_loan.pdf, p.10)

Am I responsible for paying taxes on my loan payments to the bank?

Yes, you are responsible for all goods and services taxes or other levies related to your loan. If any tax deduction is required from your payment, you must pay an additional amount to ensure the bank receives the full sum it would have otherwise received (cimb_personal_loan.pdf, p.3).

What am I responsible for if the bank incurs legal costs or losses related to my loan?

You are required to fully compensate the bank for all losses, expenses, legal fees, and other obligations—whether accidental or intentional—that arise from complaints, legal proceedings, or documents related to your loan. (standard_chartered_loan.pdf, p.8)

Can I use an electronic signature instead of a handwritten one for my loan instructions?

Yes, if the Bank agrees to accept your instruction electronically, you may provide your signature in electronic form or as an electronic image, which the Bank will treat as equivalent to your hard copy signature. (cimb_personal_loan.pdf, p.10)

What are some of the risks involved in using the internet for my loan transactions?

Risks include unauthorized data collection, use of data for criminal activity, installation of malware or viruses on your devices, hardware or network failures, phishing attempts that mimic official communications, and interception of communications through methods like "man-in-the-middle" attacks. (cimb_personal_loan.pdf, p.11)
